story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: Welcome to Python Peaks! That hooting sound is Pyra.

story.speaker: Pyra
story.message: Greetings, young coder! Every Python program starts by telling the computer to say something.

story.speaker: Pyra
story.message: We use the print() command. Type print("Hello, CodeVerse!") and the computer will display it.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: Let's give it a try in the playground!

concept.title: The print() command
concept.explanation: print() displays text on the screen. Whatever you put inside the quotes between the parentheses gets shown exactly as written.

playground.instructions: Change the text inside the quotes, then press Run to see your message appear.

challenge.prompt: Which line correctly prints the word Python?

story.speaker: Pyra
story.message: A variable is like a labeled box that stores a value for later.

story.speaker: Pyra
story.message: We write score = 10 to create a box named score holding the number 10.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: You can change what's in the box any time — just give it a new value!

concept.title: Variables
concept.explanation: A variable stores a value you can reuse and change later. Give it a clear name so your code is easy to read.

playground.instructions: Create a variable called name with your explorer name, then print it.

challenge.prompt: Fill in the blank to store the number 5 in a variable called coins.

story.speaker: Pyra
story.message: Sometimes code needs to make a choice. That's what if statements are for.

story.speaker: Pyra
story.message: if score > 50: means 'only run the next line when score is greater than 50'.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: Try changing the score and see how the message changes!

concept.title: If statements
concept.explanation: An if statement runs a block of code only when its condition is true. Indent the lines that belong to the if.

playground.instructions: Change the score value and predict whether the message will print.

challenge.prompt: if age > 12: print("Teen") — when does "Teen" print?
options: Only when age is greater than 12
Only when age is less than 12

story.speaker: Pyra
story.message: Climbing one step at a time would take forever — loops repeat actions for us!

story.speaker: Pyra
story.message: for i in range(5): repeats the next line 5 times.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: Loops save you from writing the same line over and over.

concept.title: For loops
concept.explanation: A for loop repeats a block of code a set number of times. range(5) means 'repeat 5 times'.

playground.instructions: Change the number in range() to make Pyra climb a different number of steps.

challenge.prompt: Arrange the blocks to print "Hi!" three times.

story.speaker: Pyra
story.message: You've learned variables, if, and loops. Now combine them to reach the summit!

story.speaker: Pyra
story.message: A function packages code into a reusable command using def.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: This is the Boss Challenge — show everything you've learned!

concept.title: Functions
concept.explanation: A function is a named, reusable block of code defined with def. You can call it any time by name.

playground.instructions: Write a function called celebrate that prints a victory message, then call it.

challenge.prompt: Snap the blocks to define a function called climb that prints "Up we go!" and then call it.
